verses.1: And as he entered, he continued along the holy road.
verses.2: And there was also a man who was called Zakhaios. He was the chief priest, and he was very rich.
verses.3: And he wanted to see who Jesus was. But he couldn’t do it from among the crowd, as he was too young.
verses.4: And he climbed up to the front, towards his companion, in order to see him; for he was about to pass by her.
verses.5: And when he arrived at that place, Jesus looked at him and said, “Zacharias, go away quickly! Today, I must stay in your house.”
verses.6: And he rushed down, and he welcomed him with joy.
verses.7: And all saw that he was led astray, saying that he had entered into the life of a sinner.
verses.8: But the constant Zakhai said to the lord, “See, my share of what I have is given to the poor. And if I have given anything that’s not enough, then I will give it back in full.”
verses.9: And Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has been brought to this house. For even he himself is a son of Abraham.”
verses.10: For the son of man came to seek and to save those who were lost.
verses.11: After hearing this, he added a joke, saying that Jerusalem was too small to hold the kingdom of God. It seemed like they thought that the reign of God would be short-lived.
verses.12: He said, “A noble man went to a distant land in order to establish his own kingdom there.”
verses.13: And when he called ten servants, he gave them ten minas each. Then he said to them, “Go and work in whomever I command you.”
verses.14: But his citizens rejected him and sent envoys back to him, saying, “We do not want this man to rule over us.”
verses.15: And it happened that, when he returned, he took back the kingdom from him. He also said to him, “Tell me about these slaves whom you have given silver to, so that I can know what they have done.”
verses.16: And the first person said, “Lord, it seems that time has rushed by before your eyes.”
verses.17: And he said to him, “Be good, my faithful slave. You will become very trustworthy. You will have authority over ten cities.”
verses.18: And the second one came and said, “Sir, she has made five memories.”
verses.19: And he also said to him: “You too will become one of the five cities above.”
verses.20: And the other one came and said, “Lord, look, there’s a memory of what we had in your treasury.”
verses.21: I was afraid that you might be a stubborn person. You say that I didn’t stay put, and that I didn’t fight back.
verses.22: He says to him: “I judge you from your mouth, you evil slave. You know that I am a strict man. I will not tolerate anything that is wrongful.”
verses.23: And why didn’t you give me the silver on the table? I would have used it right away, with the money I had with me.
verses.24: And to those who came forward, he said, “Take his memory away from him. And give the one who has ten memories to him.”
verses.25: And they said to him, “Lord, it has ten memories.”
verses.26: I say to you that everything belonging to those who possess it will be given to them. But those who do not possess anything will be left with nothing.
verses.27: Besides these enemies of mine, those who did not want me to become king over them, you have also brought them here and secured them in front of me.
verses.28: And as he said these things, he continued his journey forward towards Jerusalem.
verses.29: And it happened that he went to Bethphage and Bethany, towards the mountain called Elahon. He sent two of his disciples there.
verses.30: They said, “Go to the opposite village. There, you will find a door that has never been opened by anyone. Open it, then bring it here.”
verses.31: And if anyone loves you… Why do you refuse? Please understand that his Lord has a reason for this.
verses.32: And when those who were sent away arrived, they found it as he had said to them.
verses.33: And their masters said to them, “What do you mean by ‘losing the ox’?”
verses.34: But those who said that his Lord had a need for him.
verses.35: And they brought him before Jesus. After they threw their clothes over the donkey, they mounted Jesus.
verses.36: And as he walked, he kept wiping his knees with his hands along the way.
verses.37: When they were touched by him, already at the base of the oil hills, all the students began to praise the god with loud voices. They saw that there were many forces involved in this process.
verses.38: They said, “Praise be to the king who comes in the name of the Lord! May peace and glory be with him in heaven.”
verses.39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, please judge for us.”
verses.40: And after answering, he said, “I tell you that if they remain silent, then the stones will fall.”
verses.41: And as he approached, seeing the city, he rushed towards it.
verses.42: Saying that “if you knew about these things on that day, then you too would have sought peace.” But now, hide those secrets from your eyes.
verses.43: For days will come upon you, and your enemies will attack you, surround you, and trap you from all sides.
verses.44: And they will also destroy you and your children. They won’t leave a stone unturned against you, unless they know the time of your judgment.
verses.45: And when he entered the temple, he began to order the sellers to stop selling.
verses.46: I say to them: “It will be written down. And it will become my house a place of prayer. But you, you have turned it into a den of thieves.”
verses.47: And he taught every day in the temple. The high priests and the scribes tried to get rid of him, along with the first ones among the people.
verses.48: And we didn’t know what to do either, for the people were completely overwhelmed by hearing his words.
